en.name: Mentaiko
en.summary: Mentaiko and plain tarako are pollock roe sacs cured in salt, and in mentaiko's case chilli — raw, not cooked or pasteurised. Unopened, go by the printed date at 4 °C or below; once opened, 2–3 days. Frozen, 1–2 months.
en.pantry: Mentaiko belongs with sashimi in the fridge, not with preserves in the cupboard. It is raw, lightly salted roe with no heat step anywhere in its making, and the salt and chilli are seasoning. Japanese guidance is explicit that salting, vinegar, soy sauce and wasabi do not kill Anisakis larvae, so none of the seasoning here is a safety step. Keep it cold from shop to fridge, follow the 2-hour rule, and 1 hour above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Unopened, use the printed date and keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below; no general number is given because the maker's date is the honest answer for a raw cured roe. Once the pack is open, wrap each sac separately in cling film and use it within 2–3 days, a figure borrowed from what is published for fresh caviar in a jar. Keep it at the back of a shelf rather than the door, and away from anything it can perfume — mentaiko is pungent and the chilli oil travels.
en.freezer: Mentaiko freezes for 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Wrap the sacs individually, bag them and thaw in the fridge; a slow thaw keeps the grain of the roe intact. The published condition for killing Anisakis in raw seafood is −20 °C for twenty-four hours or more, and a domestic freezer at −18 °C is close but not equivalent — so buy roe sold for raw eating rather than relying on your own freezer to make it safe. Frozen mentaiko is also easier to slice thinly for pasta.
en.thawing: Thaw wrapped sacs slowly in the fridge, never at room temperature, and use them within a day. Do not refreeze.
spoilage: A sour, bitter or rancid smell over the clean salty-marine one.
A sac that has gone slimy, or liquid weeping into the pack.
Colour turning brown or dull grey rather than staying bright.
A fizzy or sharply metallic taste.
tips: Wrap each sac separately as soon as you open the pack.
Freeze what you will not eat in the next couple of days.
Slice it while part-frozen for neat rounds on pasta or rice.
Keep it well wrapped; the smell and the chilli oil get into everything.

faq.q: How long does mentaiko keep once opened?
faq.a: 2–3 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, each sac wrapped separately. Unopened, follow the printed date.
Yes, 1–2 months at −18 °C. Wrap the sacs individually and thaw slowly in the fridge.
No. It is raw roe cured in salt and chilli, with no heat step. Salt, vinegar, soy sauce and wasabi do not make raw seafood safe.

faq.q: How can you tell if mentaiko has gone off?
faq.a: A sour or rancid smell, a slimy sac, weeping liquid in the pack, or the colour turning brown or dull.

zh.name: 明太子
zh.summary: 明太子和原味鱈魚子（たらこ）都是鱈魚卵巢經鹽漬（明太子再加辣椒）而成的產品，是生的，沒有加熱也沒有殺菌。未開封請在 4 °C 以下依標示日期食用；開封後 2～3 天。冷凍 1～2 個月。
zh.pantry: 明太子在冰箱裡的位置屬於生魚片那一區，不是櫥櫃的醃漬品那一區。它是生的、輕度鹽漬的魚卵，製程中完全沒有加熱，鹽和辣椒都是調味。日本的指引明確指出：鹽漬、醋、醬油和芥末都殺不死海獸胃線蟲（Anisakis）幼蟲，所以這裡的調味沒有一項是安全步驟。從店裡到冰箱全程保冷，守 2 小時原則，室溫超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時。
zh.fridge: 未開封請以標示日期為準，並放 4 °C 以下；這裡不給通用數字，因為對生的鹽漬魚卵而言，製造商的日期就是誠實的答案。包裝一拆開，請把每條卵巢分別用保鮮膜包好，並在 2～3 天內用完，這個數字借自「玻璃瓶裝生魚子醬」的公告值。放層架深處不要放門邊，也要遠離會被染味的東西——明太子氣味強，辣油也會跑。
zh.freezer: 明太子在 −18 °C 下可放 1～2 個月。每條分開包好裝袋，解凍時放冷藏慢慢來，慢解才能保住卵粒的顆粒感。殺死生食海產中 Anisakis 的公告條件是 −20 °C 二十四小時以上，而家用冷凍庫的 −18 °C 很接近但並不等同——所以請購買標示可生食的產品，不要靠自家冷凍庫來讓它變安全。半解凍的明太子也比較好切成漂亮的薄片。
zh.thawing: 連包裝放冷藏慢慢解凍，不要放室溫，解凍後一天內用完。不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 在乾淨的鹹鮮味之外出現酸味、苦味或油耗味。
卵巢表面發黏，或包裝內滲出液體。
顏色轉褐或變得黯淡發灰，而不是鮮明。
吃起來有氣泡感或強烈金屬味。
tips: 一拆封就把每條分別包好。
這兩三天吃不完的就先冷凍。
半解凍時切片，鋪在義大利麵或飯上比較漂亮。
務必包緊；氣味和辣油會滲進所有東西。

faq.q: 明太子開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 每條分別包好放 4 °C 以下，2～3 天。未開封請依標示日期。
可以，−18 °C 下 1～2 個月。每條分開包好，放冷藏慢慢解凍。
不是。它是鹽漬加辣椒的生魚卵，沒有加熱步驟。鹽、醋、醬油和芥末都不會讓生鮮海產變安全。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷明太子壞掉了？
faq.a: 出現酸味或油耗味、表面發黏、包裝滲液，或顏色轉褐變暗。
